items.followUp: Name two other careers in biology and state what each involves.

rubric.why: Awards credit for explaining the role of medicine.
rubric.description: Medicine uses biological knowledge to diagnose, prevent or treat disease.
rubric.how: Name a relevant role of medicine.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the distinct career of surgery.
rubric.description: Surgery treats injuries or diseases by performing operations.
rubric.how: State the role of a surgeon.

rubric.why: Awards credit for defining horticulture and its practical purpose.
rubric.description: Horticulture is the cultivation and improvement of plants, such as fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants.
rubric.how: Define horticulture and give an example or purpose.

modelAnswer: Medicine applies biological knowledge to diagnose, prevent and treat diseases.
Surgery treats diseases or injuries by performing operations on the body.
Horticulture is the cultivation and improvement of plants, including fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants.
Horticulturists improve the growth and quality of useful plants.

items.followUp: Name the two main compound tissues in plants and state what each transports.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of a compound tissue.
rubric.description: A compound tissue consists of different kinds of cells working together to perform a function.
rubric.how: Define the tissue in terms of its cellular composition and shared function.

rubric.why: Checks identification and function of xylem.
rubric.description: Xylem is a compound tissue that transports water and mineral salts; it includes vessels, tracheids, fibres and parenchyma.
rubric.how: Name xylem, state what it transports, and give its cell types.

rubric.why: Checks identification and function of phloem.
rubric.description: Phloem is a compound tissue that transports prepared food; it includes sieve tubes, companion cells, fibres and parenchyma.
rubric.how: Name phloem, state what it transports, and give its cell types.

modelAnswer: A compound tissue is made of different kinds of cells that work together to perform a common function.
Xylem and phloem are the compound tissues found in vascular plants.
Xylem consists of vessels, tracheids, fibres and parenchyma; it conducts water and mineral salts.
Phloem consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, fibres and parenchyma; it transports prepared food through the plant.

items.followUp: Describe the lock-and-key model of enzyme action.

rubric.why: Checks understanding that an enzyme has a specific binding region.
rubric.description: An enzyme has a specifically shaped active site.
rubric.how: Identify the active site as the binding region.

rubric.why: Checks specificity between enzyme and substrate.
rubric.description: The substrate fits the enzyme's active site because their shapes are complementary.
rubric.how: Explain how the substrate binds to the enzyme.

rubric.why: Checks the intermediate stage of the reaction.
rubric.description: Binding forms an enzyme-substrate complex.
rubric.how: Name the intermediate complex.

rubric.why: Checks product release and enzyme reuse.
rubric.description: The reaction forms products, which leave the active site; the enzyme remains unchanged and can be reused.
rubric.how: State what happens to the products and enzyme after the reaction.

modelAnswer: Each enzyme has an active site with a particular shape.
A complementary substrate binds to the active site, forming an enzyme-substrate complex.
The enzyme catalyses the reaction and converts the substrate into product(s).
The products leave the active site, while the enzyme remains unchanged and can be used again.

items.followUp: Write the equation for aerobic respiration and describe where glycolysis occurs.

rubric.why: Checks the overall reactants and products of aerobic respiration.
rubric.description: Aerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose using oxygen, producing carbon dioxide, water and energy.
rubric.how: Write the overall word or chemical equation.

rubric.why: Checks the first stage and its location.
rubric.description: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and breaks glucose into pyruvic acid.
rubric.how: Name glycolysis, its location and its main product.

rubric.why: Checks the next stage and its location.
rubric.description: In the mitochondria, pyruvic acid is further broken down in the Krebs cycle, releasing carbon dioxide.
rubric.how: Name the Krebs cycle and state where it occurs.

rubric.why: Checks the final stage of aerobic respiration.
rubric.description: The electron transport chain operates on the inner mitochondrial membrane; oxygen accepts electrons and combines with hydrogen to form water.
rubric.how: Name the electron transport stage, its location or oxygen's role.

rubric.why: Checks the useful energy product of respiration.
rubric.description: Energy released during the stages is trapped in ATP.
rubric.how: State that respiration releases usable energy in ATP.

modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy (ATP).
First, glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and breaks glucose into pyruvic acid.
In the mitochondria, pyruvic acid is further broken down in the Krebs cycle, releasing carbon dioxide.
Electrons pass along the electron transport chain on the inner mitochondrial membrane; oxygen is the final electron acceptor and water is formed.
Energy released in these stages is captured mainly in ATP.

items.followUp: Explain why a farmer should replace mineral nutrients removed from soil by crops.

rubric.why: Checks that fertilizers supply nutrients needed by plants.
rubric.description: Fertilizers add essential mineral nutrients to the soil.
rubric.how: State what fertilizers supply.

rubric.why: Checks the role of fertilizers in maintaining soil fertility.
rubric.description: They replace mineral nutrients used up or removed by crops and help maintain soil fertility.
rubric.how: Explain how fertilizers restore soil nutrients.

rubric.why: Checks the effect of nutrient supply on plant growth.
rubric.description: Adequate mineral nutrition supports healthy plant growth and development.
rubric.how: Link nutrient supply with plant growth.

rubric.why: Checks the agricultural benefit of fertilizer use.
rubric.description: Suitable fertilizer use can increase crop yield and food production.
rubric.how: State the effect on crop production.

modelAnswer: Fertilizers supply essential mineral nutrients required for plant growth.
They replace nutrients that crops have removed from the soil and help maintain soil fertility.
Adequate mineral nutrition promotes healthy growth and development.
Using suitable fertilizers can increase crop yield and food production.

items.followUp: Compare the ways in which roots take up water and mineral ions from the soil.

rubric.why: Checks the adaptation that increases contact with soil water.
rubric.description: Root hairs provide a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions from the soil.
rubric.how: State the role of root hairs.

rubric.why: Checks the mechanism of water uptake.
rubric.description: Water enters root-hair cells by osmosis across their selectively permeable membranes.
rubric.how: Name osmosis and identify what enters by it.

rubric.why: Checks the main mechanism for mineral-ion uptake.
rubric.description: Mineral ions are often taken up by active transport, using energy, even when their concentration is lower in the soil than in root cells.
rubric.how: Name active transport and its energy requirement.

rubric.why: Checks the route taken by absorbed water toward the conducting tissue.
rubric.description: Water moves through the root cortex and enters the xylem.
rubric.how: Give the route from root hair toward the xylem.

rubric.why: Checks how water is moved onward through the plant.
rubric.description: Transpiration pull helps draw water upward through the xylem to the rest of the plant.
rubric.how: Explain the force that helps move water upward.

modelAnswer: Root hairs have a large surface area in contact with soil and absorb water and mineral ions.
Water enters root-hair cells by osmosis through their selectively permeable membranes.
Mineral ions are taken up, often by active transport, which requires energy.
Water moves through the root cortex and enters the xylem.
Transpiration pull helps draw water upward through the xylem to the rest of the plant.

items.followUp: What does the study of microbiology deal with, and how does it differ from zoology?

rubric.why: Checks the subject matter of zoology.
rubric.description: Zoology is the branch of biology concerned with animals.
rubric.how: State what zoology studies.

rubric.why: Checks the subject matter of botany.
rubric.description: Botany is the branch of biology concerned with plants.
rubric.how: State what botany studies.

modelAnswer: Zoology is the branch of biology that studies animals.
Botany is the branch of biology that studies plants.

items.followUp: Give the scientific name of wheat and state two ways it is useful to people.

rubric.why: Checks the scientific name of mustard plant.
rubric.description: The scientific name of mustard plant is Brassica campestris.
rubric.how: Write the binomial scientific name.

rubric.why: Checks the stated uses of mustard plant.
rubric.description: Mustard seeds provide oil, and mustard leaves are eaten as a vegetable.
rubric.how: Give both a seed use and a leaf use.

modelAnswer: The scientific name of mustard plant is Brassica campestris.
Its seeds provide mustard oil, and its leaves are eaten as a vegetable.
